metric.why: PPAs are how the boom finances new generation and how operators back renewable claims. Nuclear agreements, including restarts and small modular commitments, became the signature deals of the AI era.
metric.definition: Long-term contracts by which operators secure generation, nuclear, solar, wind, or gas, for current and future facilities.

reading.body:
Power purchase agreements are the financial mechanism by which data center operators lock in generation capacity, and nuclear deals have become the dominant contract type in the AI era.

PPAs function as forward commitments between operators and generators. A data center operator signs a long-term contract to purchase power from a new or existing plant, typically wind, solar, nuclear, or gas. This secures supply for both current facilities and planned expansions. The contract removes revenue risk for the generator, enabling it to finance construction. For the operator, it guarantees pricing and availability as demand grows. The prevalence of nuclear agreements specifically reflects the power density requirements of AI infrastructure, which cannot reliably scale on intermittent generation alone.

The shift toward nuclear PPAs marks a material constraint. Wind and solar contracts were the default for most cloud infrastructure. Nuclear agreements require decades-long commitments and regulatory approval, which lengthens the lead time between deciding to build a data center and the power arriving. This creates a bottleneck: operators cannot simply add capacity at will. They must negotiate generation agreements first, negotiate transmission second, then build facilities. The grid becomes the binding constraint, not the building.

This metric does not show whether agreements are being met, how many are pending, or the actual megawatts contracted. It does not measure whether nuclear plants complete on schedule, whether transmission upgrades keep pace with signed power, or the cost per megawatt-hour. It signals the financing mechanism but not its effectiveness.
